haiku-low.q1: The indexer deletes the product's document, with version = commit_lsn, so it leaves search.
haiku-low.q2: The store refuses it as a version conflict. It counts as stale, is treated as settled, and is not retried.
haiku-low.q3: It retries the same documents, waiting 1 s, 2 s, 4 s and so on, capped at 60 s. It never skips ahead, so offsets stop and the backlog grows.
haiku-low.q4: The document and error go to catalog.products.dlq, an alert is raised, and processing continues. Offsets commit after the DLQ write is acknowledged.
haiku-low.q5: Ops drop search_slot at 50 GB to protect the primary. After that, only a full rebuild brings the index back.
haiku-low.q6: The job atomically moves alias products to products_v4 once group-v4 lag is under 5 s and count is within 0.5% of active rows.
haiku-low.q7: Offsets are kept in Kafka per consumer group. They advance only after every document in the batch is settled.
haiku-low.q8: It restarts from its last committed offset and replays unsettled events. Replays are safe because the same version gives the same result.
haiku-low.q9: group-v4 starts from offsets recorded before the snapshot, applies all later events with version = commit_lsn, and keeps running past the backfill. The version rule resolves overlaps.
haiku-low.q10: Bulk-copy documents carry version = S, the WAL position read inside the snapshot.
haiku-low.q11: group-v3 keeps writing products_v3 for 48 hours, so rollback stays current. After 48 hours, group-v3 stops and products_v3 is deleted.
haiku-low.q12: Search keeps using products_v3 and products_v4 is not aliased. Restart the job: new snapshot and S, backfill resumes after the last saved id. Catch-up failure is NOT STATED.

sonnet.q1: The document is deleted from the index (c/u with status draft or archived becomes a delete, version = commit_lsn).
sonnet.q2: The older write has a lower version, so the store refuses it with a version conflict. The indexer counts it as stale, treats it as settled, does not retry, and the newer change stands.
sonnet.q3: It retries the same documents, waiting 1 s, 2 s, 4 s and so on, capped at 60 s. It never skips ahead, so offsets stop advancing and the topic backlog grows. It resumes when the index recovers.
sonnet.q4: The document and its error are written to the DLQ topic catalog.products.dlq, an alert is raised, and processing carries on. Offsets commit after the DLQ write is acknowledged. Someone must fix the cause and replay it, but the owner is unknown.
sonnet.q5: Ops drop the replication slot at 50 GB to protect the primary (alert comes at 20 GB). No new events flow in the meantime. After the slot is dropped, a full rebuild is the only way to recover search.
sonnet.q6: The reindex job moves the alias products from the old index to the new one in one atomic step. Before that, both gates must pass, checked just before the move: group-v4 lag under 5 s, and products_v4 document count within 0.5% of the active row count on the primary. There is no manual step.
sonnet.q7: In Kafka, as the consumer group's saved offsets. Offsets are committed once every document in the batch is settled (accepted, version conflict, or written to the DLQ; deleting an absent document also counts).
sonnet.q8: It restarts from its last committed offset and replays the unsettled events. Replays are safe because the same version gives the same result.
sonnet.q9: The job records the topic offsets for all 12 partitions first, then opens the snapshot and reads S. group-v4 starts from the recorded offsets and applies every event, with version = commit_lsn, in parallel with the backfill. The version rule resolves overlaps. Changes before the snapshot are in the snapshot. Changes after the offsets were recorded have events that catch-up reads.
sonnet.q10: Version = S, the WAL position read inside the snapshot.
sonnet.q11: group-v3 keeps writing to products_v3 by index name (not by alias) after the switch, so it has every change made since the switch. Rollback is moving the alias back to products_v3 in one atomic step. This lasts 48 hours. After that, group-v3 is stopped and products_v3 is deleted.
sonnet.q12: Search keeps using products_v3 through the alias, because products_v4 is not aliased until the switch. If the job crashes or its snapshot ends, it is restarted with a new snapshot and S and resumes the backfill after the last saved id, while group-v4 keeps reading from its own committed offsets. If a gate does not pass there is no switch, and an operator is alerted if the count stays off after the backfill is done.
